direction: Go NewOSKeyring writes a native item, the Rust adapter updates it, Go reads it back and deletes it: macos-latest job 'Pairing differential (macos-latest)', step 'Native keyring resource probe' (native_closeout.py keyring, live three-stage run, passed with write+verify records) on a disposable hosted runner. The digest covers the two sources that decide the macOS item address and payload encoding (keychain_status.rs, macos_keychain.rs); both are byte-identical to the attested tree bf5bd120. crates/symvault-core/src/session.rs and crates/symvault-platform/src/os_keyring.rs were exercised by the run too and are no longer digest-pinned: since bf5bd120 session.rs only wipes the wrap-key intermediates (same base64 text written under the same address) and os_keyring.rs lost its windows-only target-name branch and test (the non-windows Entry::new call is unchanged and macOS does not use that file's Keyring impl). native_keyring_interop.rs differs only by an added test (no removed line); the Rust half runs live on every disposable runner.
name: native-keyring-interop
